problem: Prior work on hallucination in LLM-based embodied agents only studies incidental cases from generic prompts or simple binary object-existence QA. It gives no systematic account of how scene-task inconsistencies trigger hallucinations in long-horizon planning.
motivation: Hallucinated objects in a plan (e.g., a nonexistent dishwasher) can cause navigation errors, unsafe actions and wasted resources in physical agents. The authors observe that inconsistency between the user instruction and the observed scene is a key trigger, so controlled inconsistencies can expose failure modes.
key_idea: Build a hallucination probing set by applying four controlled scene-task inconsistency modifications (distractor injection, task-relevant object removal, synonym substitution, scene-task contradiction) to an existing embodied benchmark's prompts, then measure hallucination across 12 LLMs.
insight: Scene-task contradiction gives the highest hallucination rates, and models show reasoning (they infer and fill in missing objects, and recognize synonyms) but cannot say 'no' to infeasible tasks. Feedback-based self-correction (SCW/KAF) leaves SceneTaskCon hallucination high, and refusal rates among non-hallucinated outputs are low (e.g., 7-20% for TaskObjRem). Absence of hallucination does not imply correct planning, since models repurpose available objects (e.g., turning on a shower instead of a washing machine). Image+text scene input reduces hallucination compared with either alone.
method: Base pipeline: the Embodied Agent Interface benchmark converts scene info and a task description into an LTL goal (node and edge goals) with an LLM goal interpreter
Distractor Injection: GPT-4o subtly inserts up to three non-existent household objects into the task description, and a hallucination is flagged if the output references them
Task Relevant Object Removal: randomly removes objects from the ground-truth LTL plan out of the scene list, and a hallucination is flagged if the removed object is referenced
Synonymous Object Substitution: GPT-4o replaces scene object names with synonyms sharing no subwords, and a hallucination is flagged if the original name reappears
Scene Task Contradiction: replaces the whole scene with objects from an unrelated scene so no required object exists, and the ideal behaviour is to abstain
Metrics: CHAIR for objects/states (fraction of hallucinated among mentioned) and POPE-style yes/no probing of non-existent objects (P_O), averaged over 3 runs
Mitigation: post-hoc self-correction using Knowledge-Augmented Feedback (generic) and Self-Correcting Woodpecker (naming the hallucinated objects)

setting.backbone: 12 LLMs evaluated frozen/prompted: Llama-3-8B, DS-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, Gemma-2-9b-it, Qwen2.5-14B, DS-R1-Distill-Qwen-14B, Llama-4-Scout-17B-16E, Llama-3.3-70B, Gemini 2.0/2.5 Flash, Mistral-Large-2411, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o; VLMs Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Llama-3.2-11B-Vision, Gemma-3-12b in a small study
setting.training_data: none (evaluation study; probing set of 2,574 prompts built on VirtualHome and BEHAVIOR tasks)
setting.observation: structured textual scene object lists (objects, states, possible states) plus a task description; images only in the small VLM study
setting.action_space: symbolic LTL goal output (node goals and edge goals); no low-level actions
setting.simulator: VirtualHome and BEHAVIOR (via Embodied Agent Interface)
setting.privileged: Ground-truth structured scene object lists are given as text input (no perception errors)

numbers_note: The paper is a hallucination study, not a navigation benchmark. It reports CHAIR/POPE hallucination rates rather than nav metrics (SR/SPL), so no canonical navigation benchmark numbers are extracted.
results: The probing set raises object hallucination up to 40x over base prompts; e.g., GPT-4o in VirtualHome goes from C_O 1.0 to 36.8 under SceneTaskCon. Gemini and Claude are the most resistant, while small models (Llama-3-8B, DS-R1-Distill-8B, Gemma-2-9b) hallucinate most. SCW reduces hallucination more than KAF, but SceneTaskCon remains high (e.g., Gemma-2-9b C_O 38.2 with SCW).
limitations: Covers only object-level hallucinations, mainly in symbolic LTL outputs, with no execution or real-world evaluation
Cross-modal experiments are small-scale and cover only Distractor Injection
Only post-hoc self-correction is tested as mitigation, and only a limited set of models is evaluated
compares_to: Base prompts of Embodied Agent Interface
version: deepread-v1 (2026-09-29): full text + insight + evidence-checked numbers
